2609.00967.title: CoBRA: Learning Tool-Use Boundaries via Counterfactual Margins
2609.00967.paper_summary: As large language models increasingly act through external tools, deciding when to call a tool has become a central problem alongside deciding how to use it. Unnecessary tool calls introduce latency, cost, retrieval noise, and error propagation, while missed calls hurt knowledge-intensive queries or questions requiring up-to-date evidence. Existing methods typically trigger tools from absolute query or generation signals, such as difficulty, confidence, or final task reward, and therefore lack an explicit estimate of the instance-level marginal benefit of tool use. We propose CoBRA, a counterfactual boundary-learning framework for tool-augmented language models. CoBRA first constructs internal and external experts from the same base model, collects paired trajectories, and estimates the reward margin between answering with and without tools. This margin partitions data into internal-favored, external-favored, and ambiguous cases. CoBRA then uses clear-margin samples for Boundary-Aware Cold-Start SFT, followed by MARS-RL with reference-split rollouts and counterfactual marginal advantages to optimize boundary decisions. Experiments with retrieval as the main tool on Qwen3-4B show that CoBRA improves tool-use efficiency and boundary-sensitive answer accuracy while maintaining strong performance on tool-dependent out-of-distribution questions.
2609.00967.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型越來越多地通過外部工具進行操作，決定何時調用工具已成為一個核心問題，與決定如何使用它並列。 不必要的工具調用會引入延遲、成本、檢索噪音和錯誤傳播，而錯過的調用則會影響知識密集型查詢或需要最新證據的問題。 現有方法通常從絕對查詢或生成信號（如難度、信心或最終任務獎勵）觸發工具，因此缺乏對工具使用的實例級邊際效益的明確估計。 我們提出了CoBRA，一種用於工具增強語言模型的反事實邊界學習框架。 CoBRA首先從相同的基礎模型構建內部和外部專家，收集配對軌跡，並估計使用工具與不使用工具之間的獎勵邊際。 這個邊際將數據劃分為內部偏好、外部偏好和模糊案例。 然後，CoBRA使用明確邊際樣本進行邊界感知冷啟動SFT，隨後進行MARS-RL，並使用參考分割的滾動和反事實邊際優勢來優化邊界決策。 在Qwen3-4B上以檢索為主要工具的實驗顯示，CoBRA提高了工具使用效率和邊界敏感的答案準確性，同時在依賴工具的分佈外問題上保持強勁的表現。
